goal: Show the developer how to make MSIX publishing consistently generate an App Installer file with the desired update policy.
must_include: For Visual Studio/packaging-project publishes, adds or renames the App Installer template item to exactly `Package.appinstaller` so the tooling consumes the desired settings; for a custom CI generator, uses a checked-in template as the source of the generated file.
Uses the App Installer 2018 namespace when relying on `ShowPrompt`, `UpdateBlocksActivation`, `AutomaticBackgroundTask`, and `ForceUpdateFromAnyVersion`.
Keeps placeholder tokens such as `{AppInstallerUri}`, `{Version}`, `{Name}`, `{Publisher}`, and `{MainPackageUri}` in the template instead of hard-coding every publish output path.
Sets `ShowPrompt="true"` when `UpdateBlocksActivation="true"`, because blocking activation is only valid with a visible update prompt.
must_not: Tells them to manually edit the generated `.appinstaller` file after every publish as the normal workflow.
Blames Visual Studio Community edition licensing for the generated update settings.
Uses the 2017/2 schema while adding settings that require the newer App Installer update schema.
Renames the template to a custom file name that the packaging project will not consume.
acceptable_alternatives: Generate the final `.appinstaller` file in CI from a checked-in template with the same schema and tokens.
Use Visual Studio's App Installer file item and edit that source template rather than the publish output.
Manage updates through Store/enterprise deployment if the organization does not want an App Installer feed.
solved: The answer tells the developer to make `Package.appinstaller` the source template consumed by Visual Studio/MSBuild, or to replace that generation with an equivalent checked-in template step, and includes the required update settings/schema so future outputs are correct automatically.
partial: The answer lists the right XML settings but does not explain where to put the template or why the generated file keeps reverting.
notes: The exact `Package.appinstaller` pickup behavior is from the accepted Stack Overflow answer; Microsoft Learn verifies update-setting semantics and minimum-version constraints.
